To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nanophasic morphologies of the amphiphilic poly(N-vinyl imidazole)-l-linked poly(tetrahydrofurane) conetworks are a function of the molecular weight of poly(tetrahydrufurane), the cross-link density and the composition of the conetwork.

the composition of the conetworks, as well as the molecular weight of both the cross-linker and the macromolecular component of the conetwork, influences the morphology of the nanophase separated conetworks.

the nanophasic morphology of poly(N-vinyl-imidazole)-l-linked by-poly(tetrihydrofuran) conetworks can be tailored by changing the composition and molecular weights of the components, and that the morphology is also affected by the molecular weight of macromolecular crosslinker.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization, and morphology of poly(N-vinyl imidazole)-l-Poly(tetrahydofuran) (PVim-l-PTHF).

the synthesis and investigation of the structure–property relationships in PVIm-l-PTHFDMA conetworks, which are promising candidates to be used as drug delivery systems and nanoreactors for the preparation of nanomaterials.

the preparation of a new class of amphiphilic polymeric materials and the investigation of the structure–property relationship of these materials in the context of the composition, molecular weight, and cross-linking density.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nanophasic morphology in the poly(N-vinylimidazole)-l-p-tetrahydrofurfuryl dimethacrylate amphiphilic polymeric conetworks (PVIm-l-PtHFDMA APCNs) is strongly influenced by the composition and molecular mass of the components.

the composition of the APCNs and the molecular weight and functionality of the macromonomer have a significant influence on the phase separation and the morphology of the nanophase separated PVIm-l-PTHFDMA APCNs.

the nanophasic morphology is strongly affected by the composition and the molecular weight, but the morphology is independent of the molecular weight of PVIm and the molecular weight distribution of PTHF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the composition and molecular weights of the cross-linker and the polymer segments in APCNs have a profound effect on the formation of different nanophasic morphologies and the resulting properties of the APCNs.

the nanophasic morphology of the APCNs can be controlled by the composition and molecular weights of the components and the morphology of the conetworks can be tuned in a broad range of compositions by varying the molecular weights of the cross-linker.

the nanophasic morphologies of these amphiphilic polymeric materials can be controlled by the conetwork composition and molecular weight, and the resulting nanostructures can be utilized for various applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the formation of the bicontinuous morphology is possible in broad composition ranges and the molecular weight has a significant influence on the size of the domains and the distance between the phases.
the formation of a broad variety of morphologies in these APCNs is possible in a broad composition and molecular weight range of the components.

it shows that a broad composition range of the amphiphilic poly(N-vinylimidazole)-l-p-tetrahydrofurfuryl dimethacrylate (PVIm-l-pTHFDMA) conetworks can be synthesized with a bicontinous (cocontinuous) morphology in the nanosize range.
